content:
Apple today announced the first eight performances at the newly opened Apple Music Hall in London, with Elton John kicking things off next week. Here are the details.

Elton John to headline opening night at Apple Music Hall

Earlier this week, Apple unveiled Apple Music Hall, a brand-new concert venue located at London's iconic Battersea Power Station, where Apple also has offices and a retail store.

Apple Music Hall can hold up to 600 people, and performances will be live-streamed globally via Apple Music. Performers will also receive finished Spatial Audio recordings, ready-to-broadcast mixes, and multi-camera video.

When Apple first announced Apple Music Hall, it said it would soon reveal the first artists to perform at the venue.

Today Apple confirmed the line-up for the first eight performances, with next week's Elton John taking the opening slot. Here is the full list:

  • Elton John — September 28
  • Baby Keem — October 2
  • Skye Newman — October 7
  • Troye Sivan — October 13
  • Arlo Parks — October 22
  • Burna Boy — October 29
  • Chase & Status — November 26
  • Charli xcx — December 2

Some of the artists have deep ties to Apple Music. Take Elton John, for instance — he has hosted the weekly "Rocket Hour" radio show since Apple Music launched in 2015; meanwhile, Charli xcx previously hosted five seasons of her own show "The Candy Shop" on Beats 1.

On the concert front, Apple says "tickets for Elton John, Baby Keem and Skye Newman will go on sale at 9 a.m. BST on Monday, September 28," while "on-sale dates for all remaining shows will be announced later."

For more information about tickets and availability, click this link.

Apple Music requires an active subscription. You can subscribe for $11.99 per month, with the first month free, or bundle it through an Apple One subscription.
